The schemas in these tests eventually reach `marshmallow.fields._TemporalField._deserialize` (file `src/marshmallow/fields.py`) through `Field.deserialize` and container fields.

Scope: every function/method whose `def` appears DIRECTLY in the class body of one of these six classes in `src/marshmallow/fields.py`: `_TemporalField`, `DateTime`, `NaiveDateTime`, `AwareDateTime`, `Time`, `Date`. This includes `__init__`, dunder methods, staticmethods and abstract methods defined there (whether or not they can ever execute). Inherited methods are NOT re-listed under a subclass: a method belongs only to the class whose body textually defines it (e.g. a call to `DateTime(...).method` that resolves to `_TemporalField.method` counts toward `_TemporalField.method`). Methods of other classes (e.g. `Field`, `List`, `Schema`) and functions in other files are out of scope. There are no nested functions, lambdas, or properties inside these six class bodies, so none are tracked.

Identity: `func` is the dotted `module.qualname` of the function, where the module is `marshmallow.fields`, e.g. `marshmallow.fields.Field.serialize` (format example only; that method is not in scope). `file` is the repo-relative path `src/marshmallow/fields.py` for every entry.

Counting: one invocation = one Python `call` event (a new frame created for that function's code object), regardless of who called it (the test, another in-scope method via `super()`, marshmallow internals, a container field, etc.) and regardless of whether the call returns normally or raises. Recursive/re-entrant calls each count. None of the in-scope functions are generators, so no resumption issue arises. Count only during the execution of the test methods themselves (class bodies of the test-local Schema classes are evaluated inside the test method and so any calls they trigger count; module import of marshmallow does not).

Zero rule: every in-scope function appears exactly once in the answer, with `count: 0` if it never ran.

Aggregation: counts are summed across all test methods of the class.

Output: `{"invocation_counts": [{"count": int, "file": str, "func": str}, ...]}`, sorted by `func` ascending (plain Python string ordering, so uppercase letters sort before `_`); qualnames are unique, so no tie-break is needed.
